For FOL statement 9, `∀x (¬p_15(x) ∨ p_6(x))` is equivalent to `∀x (p_15(x) → p_6(x))`. This translates to 'For all x, if x compromises their values, then x loses self-respect.' The corresponding FOL for NL would be `∀x (p_15(x) ∨ p_6(x))` if interpreted as `¬(¬p_15(x)) ∨ p_6(x)`.

For FOL statement 10, `∀x (¬p_15(x) ∨ p_7(x))` is equivalent to `∀x (p_15(x) → p_7(x))`. This translates to 'For all x, if x compromises their values, then x damages their reputation.' The NL statement says 'if x *does not* compromise their values', which corresponds to `∀x (¬p_15(x) → p_7(x))`. The corresponding FOL for NL would be `∀x (p_15(x) ∨ p_7(x))` if interpreted as `¬(¬p_15(x)) ∨ p_7(x).`

Both cases involve a misunderstanding of how `¬A ∨ B` translates to an 'if-then' statement. `¬A ∨ B` means 'If A, then B'. The NL implies 'If NOT A, then B', which would be `¬(¬A) ∨ B` or `A ∨ B` if written as disjunction, or `¬A → B` if written as implication.
